title: Гипоадренокортицизм
terminology: Addison disease strictly denotes primary hypoadrenocorticism; secondary and iatrogenic adrenal insufficiency remain related but distinct routes.
Waxing and waning gastrointestinal, lethargy, weakness and weight changes are nonspecific but become meaningful in a preserved longitudinal pattern.
Hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, low Na:K ratio, azotemia, hypoglycemia and absent stress leukogram support suspicion but are not individually pathognomonic.
Normal sodium and potassium do not exclude glucocorticoid-deficient primary or secondary disease.
An appropriate resting cortisol can rule out disease, but a low value cannot confirm it.
Definitive confirmation requires an interpretable ACTH stimulation test with sample, timing and exogenous-steroid context preserved.
Primary, secondary and mineralocorticoid classification follows confirmation and can remain uncertain pending specialist review.
In crisis, life-saving stabilization proceeds while diagnostic samples are preserved when possible and never waits for every result.
Fluid-responsive azotemia or dramatic improvement alone does not prove Addison disease; kidney, GI, sepsis and other mimics remain.
Every glucocorticoid route and Cushing-treatment exposure is inventoried; abrupt withdrawal is unsafe.
Stable replacement monitoring uses individual symptoms, weight and electrolytes rather than one universal interval.
No fluid, electrolyte, glucocorticoid, mineralocorticoid, stress-dose, ACTH-test or emergency protocol is generated.

commonHistoryQuestions.prompt: Были ли эпизоды vomiting, diarrhea, lethargy и связь со stress?
Как менялись weight, appetite, water и urine?
Есть ли сейчас collapse, weakness, melena или tremor?
Какие glucocorticoid routes и Cushing treatments использовались?
Каковы прошлые sodium, potassium, glucose, creatinine и urine results?
Каковы baseline cortisol или ACTH protocol, sample, timing и result?
Были ли missed replacement, новая illness или stress event?
Как менялись perfusion и azotemia после fluids без диагностического вывода?
Есть ли renal, GI, parasite, protein-losing или sepsis evidence?
Подтверждались ли primary, secondary или mineralocorticoid status?
Как фактически выполняется replacement и есть ли signs of deficiency/excess?
Есть ли reviewed emergency plan, teach-back, transport и referral access?

sourceCatalog.title: Merck Veterinary Manual: Addison Disease in Animals

variants.title: Первичный гипоадренокортицизм с mineralocorticoid deficiency
variants.diagnosticTruth: Primary hypoadrenocorticism with mineralocorticoid deficiency is suspected from a preserved waxing/waning clinical and supportive routine-lab/electrolyte pattern, but Na:K, azotemia, hypoglycemia, breed and fluid response are not diagnostic; confirmation requires interpretable ACTH stimulation and mimic review.

presentations.complaint: Recurrent vomiting, diarrhea, poor appetite, lethargy and weight loss wax and wane, often around stress.

historyAnswers.episodic_gi_lethargy_and_stress_triggers: Repeat episodes and stress association fixed.
historyAnswers.weight_appetite_water_urine_trend: Weight/appetite decline and variable water/urine recorded.

examFindings.finding: Episodes remain one patient trajectory.
GI, renal, parasite and protein-losing routes remain.

followUp.timing: after core/mimic review and ACTH confirmation route

outcomes.safe: The longitudinal pattern prompts a complete confirmatory route.
outcomes.unsafe: Vague GI signs or breed alone become Addison disease.

ownerCommunication: Explain that the recurring pattern matters, but several diseases can imitate it.

presentations.complaint: Hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, azotemia, hypoglycemia or a low Na:K ratio accompanies compatible illness.

examFindings.finding: Na:K cannot pass confirmation gate.
Emergency stabilization may precede final diagnosis.

followUp.timing: continuous if unstable then ACTH and classification checkpoint

outcomes.safe: Dangerous abnormalities are stabilized while ACTH confirmation remains required.
outcomes.unsafe: A ratio or rapid fluid response is treated as diagnostic proof.

ownerCommunication: Explain that the pattern is concerning and urgent but still needs a confirmatory hormone test.

presentations.complaint: Renal, gastrointestinal, parasitic, protein-losing, septic or other chronic disease can reproduce part of the Addison pattern.

examFindings.finding: No great-imitator shortcut.
Response changes physiology, not diagnosis alone.

outcomes.safe: The endocrine and mimic routes remain simultaneously testable.
outcomes.unsafe: A dramatic response or low ratio erases renal/GI/septic disease.

ownerCommunication: Explain why Addison is called an imitator and which test separates it from current alternatives.

variants.title: Eunatremic/eukalemic primary или secondary hypoadrenocorticism
variants.diagnosticTruth: Normal sodium and potassium do not exclude isolated glucocorticoid-deficient primary or secondary hypoadrenocorticism; a low resting cortisol requires ACTH confirmation, after which primary/secondary classification and possible future mineralocorticoid evolution are monitored.

presentations.complaint: Recurrent GI signs, weakness or weight loss persist despite normal sodium and potassium.

historyAnswers.prior_sodium_potassium_glucose_creatinin: Normal electrolytes documented, not assumed exclusion.

examFindings.finding: Primary isolated or secondary routes remain.
Normal electrolytes do not create random ACTH testing.

followUp.timing: ACTH conclusion then classification and electrolyte evolution

outcomes.safe: Nonclassic disease remains discoverable without indiscriminate testing.
outcomes.unsafe: Normal electrolytes falsely close the endocrine route.

ownerCommunication: Explain that normal sodium and potassium remove one clue but not all forms of cortisol deficiency.

presentations.complaint: A low resting cortisol is found in an appropriate patient but cannot confirm hypoadrenocorticism.

examFindings.finding: Treatment activation blocked pending ACTH evidence.
No isolated number shortcut.

followUp.timing: timed ACTH confirmation without unsafe delay if unstable

outcomes.safe: The low-cost screen appropriately leads to definitive confirmation.
outcomes.unsafe: A low resting value activates diagnosis or treatment directly.

ownerCommunication: Explain that a high-enough result can rule disease out, but a low result has many causes and needs ACTH testing.

presentations.complaint: ACTH-confirmed glucocorticoid deficiency needs primary-versus-secondary classification and future electrolyte monitoring.

examFindings.finding: Post-confirmation evidence required.
Mineralocorticoid deficiency may evolve.

followUp.timing: post-confirmation classification and individualized electrolyte trajectory

outcomes.safe: Classification and possible evolution remain explicit and longitudinal.
outcomes.unsafe: Every normal-electrolyte case is permanently labeled atypical primary disease.

ownerCommunication: Explain why confirming cortisol deficiency and identifying its cause are two separate steps.

variants.title: Аддисонический криз
variants.diagnosticTruth: Addisonian crisis is a life-threatening hypovolemic/metabolic state requiring immediate perfusion, ECG, glucose, electrolyte and acid-base stabilization; diagnostic samples are preserved when possible but treatment does not wait, and AKI, sepsis, GI catastrophe and other mimics remain until confirmed.

presentations.complaint: Collapse, hypotension/hypovolemia or severe vomiting/diarrhea creates an Addisonian-crisis differential.

historyAnswers.episodic_gi_lethargy_and_stress_triggers: Prior episodic pattern retained if available.

examFindings.finding: Samples are preserved only when they do not delay care.
Hospital/ICU or safe transfer required.

followUp.timing: continuous stabilization through ICU handoff then confirmation/classification

outcomes.safe: Emergency care and diagnostic preservation proceed in parallel.
outcomes.unsafe: The patient waits or goes home for an external result.

ownerCommunication: State that shock treatment must start now while the endocrine diagnosis is confirmed in parallel.

presentations.complaint: Hyperkalemic bradyarrhythmia, hypoglycemia, acidosis or rapidly changing electrolytes accompany suspected crisis.

examFindings.finding: Repeated by clinical need, not a fixed generated schedule.
Engine provides route, not regimen.

outcomes.safe: Physiologic threats drive reviewed emergency care without delaying confirmation.
outcomes.unsafe: The engine invents correction rates, fluid choices or hormone doses.

ownerCommunication: Explain that the immediate risks are heart rhythm, blood sugar and shock while the cause is confirmed.

presentations.complaint: AKI, sepsis, GI catastrophe, hemorrhage or other shock state mimics an Addisonian crisis.

examFindings.finding: Endocrine suspicion does not suppress sepsis/AKI/GI routes.
Same response can occur in hypovolemia of other causes.

followUp.timing: continuous shared-shock assessment until cause and trajectory are established

outcomes.safe: All dangerous mimics stay visible until decisive evidence.
outcomes.unsafe: Response to fluids alone closes the case as Addison disease.

ownerCommunication: Explain that several emergencies look alike initially and must be treated while tests separate them.

variants.title: Ятрогенная супрессия или продольное ведение
variants.diagnosticTruth: Iatrogenic adrenal suppression and stable longitudinal replacement are distinct from primary Addison disease; all-route exposure and Cushing-treatment history, individualized clinical/weight/electrolyte monitoring and a reviewed illness/stress/missed-dose emergency plan preserve continuity without generated dosing or intervals.

presentations.complaint: Glucocorticoid withdrawal or Cushing treatment precedes signs compatible with HPA-axis suppression.

historyAnswers.all_glucocorticoid_and_cushing_treatment: Every route, treatment and change fixed.
historyAnswers.current_replacement_actual_use_and_adver: Actual use and deficiency/excess signs recorded.

examFindings.finding: Cause and mineralocorticoid expectations remain separate.
Reviewed plan required.

followUp.timing: reviewed treatment-change and axis/clinical safety checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Suppression is recognized without mislabeling primary Addison or inventing a taper.
outcomes.unsafe: The engine declares abrupt withdrawal safe or generates replacement.

ownerCommunication: Explain that medication-related suppression can mimic Addison but has a different cause and plan.

presentations.complaint: A confirmed stable patient requires individualized replacement-response, weight and electrolyte monitoring.

historyAnswers.current_replacement_actual_use_and_adver: Actual plan and deficiency/excess signs fixed.

examFindings.finding: No universal schedule generated.
One number cannot dictate the whole plan.

followUp.timing: individual reviewed interval with home and laboratory checkpoints

outcomes.safe: Monitoring adapts to the same patient's response and safety.
outcomes.unsafe: Every dog receives one generated interval or adjustment rule.

ownerCommunication: Explain which home signs and laboratory trends determine the next reviewed checkpoint.

presentations.complaint: New illness, stress or missed replacement requires a reviewed emergency plan, red-flag triage and owner teach-back.

historyAnswers.missed_replacement_new_illness_or_stress: Exact event, timing and signs fixed.
historyAnswers.current_replacement_actual_use_and_adver: Actual plan use reconciled without blame.

examFindings.finding: Event depends on authored exposure, time and state.
Engine surfaces route/red flags, not dose.

followUp.timing: event-specific urgent contact then post-event plan teach-back

outcomes.safe: The owner uses a reviewed patient-specific plan with visible emergency thresholds.
outcomes.unsafe: The UI invents a stress dose or produces random unrelated collapse.

ownerCommunication: Use teach-back: ask the owner to describe whom to contact and which signs mean immediate emergency care.

familyValidationRules: Reject if Na:K, breed, low baseline cortisol or fluid response alone proves disease.
Reject if normal electrolytes exclude hypoadrenocorticism or secondary/iatrogenic disease is mislabeled primary Addison disease.
Reject if crisis waits for all results before stabilization or is discharged awaiting an external test.
Reject if exogenous steroid/Cushing-treatment exposure is omitted or abrupt withdrawal is safe.
Reject if monitoring uses one universal interval or a missed dose creates an unrelated random patient event.
Reject if code generates fluid, electrolyte, glucocorticoid/mineralocorticoid, stress-dose or ACTH-test protocol.
